paper_sections.title: Subjective Rating and EMG Data Acquisition and Analysis
Action‐Dependent Information Within a Distributed Network Over the PMC and the PPC

description.value: An fMRI MVPA study decoding the content of imagined right-hand actions from BOLD activity patterns in frontal, parietal, motor, and visual regions.

spans.text: The current study addresses the question whether different types of imagined hand actions can be decoded from spatial patterns of BOLD signals in motor and motor‐related cortices.

description.value: Within-subject, pseudo-randomized and counterbalanced experiment with 20 right-handed volunteers; participants completed 20 runs of four conditions and were scanned for approximately 50 minutes.

spans.text: Conditions were presented in a pseudo‐randomized order counterbalanced across subjects.
Each subject performed 20 runs of eight trials each (corresponding to two trials in each of the four conditions)
The study was approved by the local ethics committee

value: Imagined hand actions could be decoded from activity patterns in left M1 and PMC, right SPL, bilateral motor and visual cortex, and human motion complex/extrastriate body area regions.

spans.text: This analysis confirmed that imagined hand actions could be decoded from activity patterns in left M1 and PMC, as well as right SPL (with one significant cluster in the left precentral gyrus, two in the left SMA, and one in right SPL). In addition, the searchlight analysis revealed significant clusters in right motor cortices (two stretching across pre‐ and postcentral gyrus, one in the SMA) and bilateral early visual cortex (EVC; two in the right hemisphere and one large cluster stretching from left EVC to left SPL), as well as bilateral human motion complex (V5/hMT+) and/or the extrastriate body area (EBA; left and right cluster stretching into fusiform gyrus and IPL, respectively; left peak coordinates being very close to EBA coordinates reported by Downing et al. [ 2001 ]).

description.value: Participants imagined right-hand squeezing, aiming, or extension–flexion actions, interleaved with rest, while undergoing fMRI.

spans.text: In the MI conditions, they were instructed to imagine either a force production task squeezing a bellows, an aiming task pointing with the index finger at five targets affixed to the bellows, or an extension  –  flexion movement with the right hand (i.e., the fingers) alongside the bellows.
